title: Prime Gaps Are Unbounded
description: An elementary factorial-construction proof that gaps between consecutive primes grow without bound, in two forms: for every G there is a block of G consecutive composites (G+1)!+2,…,(G+1)!+(G+1) (exists_consecutive_composites), and there exist consecutive primes p < q with q − p ≥ G (exists_large_prime_gap). This discharges the large_prime_gaps_exist statement that had appeared only as an axiom in Erdos454Problem. No analytic number theory needed. 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: That gaps between consecutive primes can be arbitrarily large is one of the oldest elementary observations in number theory, traditionally credited to the factorial construction that already appears in nineteenth-century textbooks: the $G$ consecutive integers $(G+1)!+2,\dots,(G+1)!+(G+1)$ are all composite because $j\mid(G+1)!+j$ for each $2\le j\le G+1$. It stands in deliberate contrast to the deep *small-gap* side of the spectrum — Zhang's 2013 breakthrough and the Maynard–Tao method proving bounded gaps $\liminf(p_{n+1}-p_n)<\infty$ — which the gallery already develops under `bounded-prime-gaps`. Large gaps, by contrast, need no analytic machinery at all: the factorial block gives them outright, and the finer quantitative question (how large gaps must be infinitely often, the Erdős–Rankin problem answered by Ford–Green–Konyagin–Maynard–Tao in 2014) is a separate story. In this project the unboundedness statement had appeared only as an unproved `axiom` (`large_prime_gaps_exist` in `Erdos454Problem.lean`); this file discharges it with a fully machine-checked elementary argument, 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
overview.problemStatement: Formalise, elementarily and with no analytic number theory, that prime gaps are unbounded: for every $G$ produce a run of $G$ consecutive composites, and produce two *consecutive* primes $p<q$ (no prime strictly between them) with $q-p\ge G$, thereby discharging the previously axiomatised `large_prime_gaps_exist`.
overview.proofStrategy: One divisibility lemma carries the whole proof: for $2\le j\le G+1$, $j$ divides $(G+1)!+j$ with $1<j<(G+1)!+j$, so $(G+1)!+j$ is composite (`not_prime_factorial_add`). Ranging $j$ over $2,\dots,G+1$ gives $G$ consecutive composites (`exists_consecutive_composites`). For the consecutive-prime form, sandwich this prime-free block: take $q$ the least prime $\ge (G+1)!+2$ via `Nat.find` on `exists_infinite_primes` (forced $\ge (G+1)!+G+2$ because the block is prime-free) and $p$ the greatest prime $\le(G+1)!+1$ via `Nat.findGreatest`, then check nothing prime lies strictly between them.
keyInsights: A single divisibility fact does everything: $j\mid(G+1)!$ whenever $j\le G+1$, so $j\mid(G+1)!+j$, and the strict bounds $1<j<(G+1)!+j$ make the divisor nontrivial — hence $(G+1)!+j$ is composite.
The factorial $(G+1)!$ is the cheapest number simultaneously divisible by every $j\in\{2,\dots,G+1\}$, which is exactly why shifting it by $j$ manufactures composites in a contiguous block.
Unboundedness of *large* gaps is elementary and needs no analysis, in sharp contrast to the *bounded* (small) gaps side (Zhang / Maynard–Tao) developed elsewhere in the gallery.

Turning 'a run of composites exists' into 'consecutive primes far apart exist' is a sandwiching argument: the least prime above the block (`Nat.find`) and the greatest prime below it (`Nat.findGreatest`) are automatically consecutive, and the prime-free block forces their gap $\ge G$.
`Nat.find` on `Nat.exists_infinite_primes` supplies a *minimal* prime $\ge M+2$ together with its minimality certificate, which is what proves no prime sits inside the block.

The proof discharges a statement that had been assumed as an `axiom` (`large_prime_gaps_exist`), removing an assumption from the project's dependency graph while keeping the argument fully constructive.

sections.title: Preamble: imports, statement, motivation
sections.summary: Header and module docstring stating the goal (prime gaps are unbounded, in two forms), the contrast with the gallery's `bounded-prime-gaps` small-gap development, the note that unboundedness had appeared only as the `large_prime_gaps_exist` axiom, and the factorial construction. Imports basic factorial/prime lemmas and `Nat.Find`; opens `namespace PrimeGapsUnbounded`.

sections.title: not_prime_factorial_add: the composite witness
sections.summary: The one workhorse lemma: for $2\le j\le G+1$, $(G+1)!+j$ is not prime. Uses `Nat.not_prime_iff_exists_dvd_ne` and exhibits $j$ as a nontrivial divisor via `dvd_add (Nat.dvd_factorial …) (dvd_refl j)`, with the strict inequalities closed by `omega`.

sections.title: exists_consecutive_composites: arbitrarily long runs
sections.summary: For every $G$ produces $m=(G+1)!+2$ such that $m,m+1,\dots,m+(G-1)$ are all composite. Reindexes $m+i=(G+1)!+(i+2)$ and applies `not_prime_factorial_add` to each, giving $G$ consecutive composites.

sections.title: exists_large_prime_gap: prime-free block and the prime above
sections.summary: States the consecutive-prime form. Establishes that the block $[M+2,M+G+1]$ (with $M=(G+1)!$) is prime-free (`hrun`), then takes $q$ = the least prime $\ge M+2$ via `Nat.find` on `exists_infinite_primes`, whose minimality plus the prime-free block force $q\ge M+G+2$.

sections.title: The prime below and the consecutive-prime assembly
sections.summary: Takes $p$ = the greatest prime $\le M+1$ via `Nat.findGreatest` (nonzero because 2 is prime and $\le M+1$), then assembles: $p<q$, $p+G\le q$, and no prime strictly between them — case-splitting a candidate $k$ against $M+1$ and invoking `hp_greatest` or `hq_min` accordingly.

sections.title: Worked demonstrations
sections.summary: Two `example`s instantiating the theorems: 100 consecutive composite numbers, and a pair of consecutive primes differing by at least 1000 — concrete sanity checks that the general statements fire.

conclusion.summary: Prime gaps are unbounded, proved elementarily in two forms with 0 axioms and 0 sorries: `exists_consecutive_composites` gives, for every $G$, a run of $G$ consecutive composites $(G+1)!+2,\dots,(G+1)!+(G+1)$, and `exists_large_prime_gap` gives consecutive primes $p<q$ with $q-p\ge G$. The entire argument rests on the single divisibility lemma `not_prime_factorial_add`.
conclusion.implications: The file discharges `large_prime_gaps_exist`, previously an unproved `axiom` in `Erdos454Problem.lean`, removing an assumption from the project. It also frames the gallery's prime-gap coverage as two-sided: the elementary *large*-gap side here versus the deep *small*-gap `bounded-prime-gaps` (Maynard–Tao) development. The consecutive-prime sandwich technique (`Nat.find` above, `Nat.findGreatest` below) is a reusable pattern for extracting adjacent primes around any prime-free interval.
openQuestions: Can the quantitative Erdős–Rankin lower bound on the largest gap below $x$ (Ford–Green–Konyagin–Maynard–Tao 2014) be formalised, moving beyond mere unboundedness?
Does the same `Nat.find`/`Nat.findGreatest` sandwich give an effective bound on where the first gap $\ge G$ occurs, rather than only its existence?
Can `exists_consecutive_composites` be sharpened to the smaller Jacobsthal-style starting points instead of $(G+1)!$?

crossReferences.description: The complementary *small*-gap development (admissible tuples, Maynard–Tao, bounded gaps). This entry treats the opposite, *large*-gap side of the same spectrum, elementarily.
Relies on the infinitude of primes (`Nat.exists_infinite_primes`) to locate the least prime above the composite block; the factorial construction here echoes Euclid's factorial-based argument.
Home of the `large_prime_gaps_exist` axiom that this file discharges with a machine-checked elementary proof.

references.title: An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers
references.author: G. H. Hardy and E. M. Wright
references.venue: Oxford University Press (6th ed., rev. Heath-Brown, Silverman, Wiles)
references.description: Classical treatment of the distribution of primes; the elementary fact that gaps between consecutive primes are unbounded, established without analytic input, is standard textbook material here.

references.title: Elementary Number Theory and Its Applications
references.author: Kenneth H. Rosen
references.description: Presents the factorial-block construction explicitly: the G consecutive integers (G+1)!+2, …, (G+1)!+(G+1) are each composite, giving arbitrarily long prime-free runs — exactly the argument formalized as exists_consecutive_composites.

references.title: On the difference of consecutive primes
references.author: Paul Erdős
references.venue: Quarterly Journal of Mathematics, Oxford Series, 6, 124–128
references.description: Origin of the quantitative study of large prime gaps (the Erdős–Rankin lower bound), the deep refinement beyond the mere unboundedness proved here and cited in this entry's open questions.
